items.title: For a local complete intersection morphism the shriek of the structure sheaf is invertible and the shriek preserves perfect complexes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-shriek, for a local complete intersection morphism f : X -> Y of FTS_S, the lemma asserts that f^!O_Y is an invertible object of D(O_X) and that f^! maps perfect complexes to perfect complexes (statement lines 4908-4917). The proof recalls that a local complete intersection morphism is perfect by More on Morphisms, Lemma labelled more-morphisms-lemma-lci-properties, and that by Lemma labelled lemma-perfect-comparison-shriek it suffices to show the invertibility statement (proof lines 4919-4925). The question is local, so one may assume X -> Y factors as X -> A^n_Y -> Y with the first arrow a Koszul regular immersion by More on Morphisms, Section labelled more-morphisms-section-lci; the affine line case is Lemma labelled lemma-shriek-affine-line, leaving the case of a Koszul regular immersion (proof lines 4927-4936). Working locally once more the proof reduces to X = Spec(A), Y = Spec(B) with A = B/(f_1, ..., f_r) for a regular sequence, using that Koszul regular and regular agree for Noetherian local rings by More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-noetherian-finite-all-equivalent, so that the morphism decomposes as a chain of effective Cartier divisor inclusions (proof lines 4938-4947). For a single effective Cartier divisor i : D -> X one has i^!O_X = N[1] by Lemma labelled lemma-compute-for-effective-Cartier, which is invertible, and the proof is complete (proof lines 4949-4951). Reducing to a chain of Cartier divisors and computing the top case is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
